@: English source texts of the download page. Keys starting with @ are notes for translators (the page ignores them). See i18n/README.md for the rules: {placeholders} stay as they are, <strong>/<em>/<code> may move but stay balanced, the glossary names stay in English.

status.title: Game server status
@status.pill.offline: The small pill at the top right, next to a coloured dot: as short as possible, it has to fit on a phone.
@status.tip.online-pilots: Tooltip of the pill. {pilots} is status.pilots ("12 pilots online").
status.tip.offline: The game server is not answering
@status.inline.wrap: Brackets around the server's state in the Game server help card: "… connects to https://… (online)." {state} is one of status.inline.* or status.pilots.
@status.pilots: Plural: write the forms your language needs (see README). {n} is the number, already formatted.
@hero.eyebrow: Small capitals above the game's name (the game's landing.card.edition says the beta part).
hero.lede: Fly for a corporation, hunt aliens with your clan and climb the season ranking. A native game for macOS, Windows and Linux.
@hero.lede: The first sentence is the game's own pitch (landing.card.pitch): use its translation.
@hero.download-for: The big button when we know the visitor's system. {platform} is macOS, Windows or Linux.
@hero.download-mobile: The big button on a phone or tablet: it jumps to the download list.
@hero.sub.linux: Second line of the big button, under hero.download-for.
hero.note: Free download. Needs an internet connection: the game plays on the SpaceCorps server.
hero.note-mobile: SpaceCorps 2027 is a desktop game for macOS, Windows and Linux.
shots.title: In the game
shots.lede: Real frames from the client, rendered by its own engine.
shots.combat.alt: Flight: the pilot's ship trades laser fire with a shielded Seeker alien over a red nebula, a ringed planet behind them and the HUD around the edges.
@shots.combat.alt: Image descriptions (alt) are read aloud by screen readers. Seeker, Wraith, Protos: names from the game, keep them.
shots.combat.caption: Combat in sector M-1: lasers, return fire and shields against a Seeker.
shots.station.alt: The pilot's ship flying over the giant ring of the Mission Control station, an explosion flaring on its hull.
shots.station.caption: Mission Control, the company's station
@shots.station.caption: Mission Control is the station's name in the game: keep it.
shots.wraith.alt: The in-game wiki's Wraith page: the painted battleship turning on a holographic pad beside its specifications.
shots.wraith.caption: The Wraith in the wiki's model viewer
shots.hangar.alt: The hangar: a Protos in its bay, combat stats, laser and generator slots, and the inventory.
shots.hangar.caption: Hangar: ships, configurations, equipment
shots.galaxy.alt: The galaxy map: the three companies' sectors linked by jump routes around the PvP sectors in the middle.
shots.galaxy.caption: The star system: company sectors around the PvP core
features.title: What's in it
features.lede: The SpaceCorps MMO, rebuilt as a native desktop game.
features.ships.title: Painted ships
features.ships.text: Protos, Paragon, Wraith and Ostirion carry their own liveries, panel lines, hull numbers and blinking navigation lights.
features.combat.title: Real-time combat
features.combat.text: Lasers, rockets, shields and drones against five alien species and other pilots, simulated by an authoritative server.
features.corporations.title: Three corporations
features.corporations.text: Fly for Mars Colonization, Terra Space Group or Galactic Ventures, and push into the PvP sectors at the heart of the map.
@features.corporations.text: The three corporations' names stay in English.
features.clans.title: Clans
features.clans.text: Found or join a clan: members and ranks, a shared bank, clan levels, and diplomacy from treaties to war.
features.seasons.title: Seasons
features.seasons.text: Thirty days from a fresh start to the Blackhole Eruption. Wipe points buy permanent boosts that outlast the reset.
@features.seasons.text: The Blackhole Eruption is the event that ends a season (the universe wipe). Wipe points: see the glossary.
features.gates.title: Galaxy Gates
features.gates.text: Materialize the 100 parts of the Chrono-Gate to open the Transport Cache and pick next season's sector.
@features.gates.text: Chrono-Gate is a name (never translated). The Transport Cache keeps items through the season's wipe.
features.crafting.title: Crafting
features.crafting.text: Craft and fuse equipment in the Assembly, and run Skylab station modules that produce resources.
@features.crafting.text: Assembly is a station page of the game (crafting and fusion). Skylab is a name.
features.languages.title: Ten languages
features.languages.text: English, Deutsch, Español, Français, Português, Svenska, Русский, 日本語, 한국어 and 简体中文.
@features.languages.text: Keep every language's own name as written; translate only the list's commas and "and".

help.title: First launch
help.lede: The builds aren't signed by Apple or Microsoft yet, so your system asks once before it opens the game.
help.macos.title: macOS: "can't be opened" or "not verified"
@help.macos.install: Bold and italic words in the help are what the player sees on screen: use the names macOS and Windows show in your language (Applications is Programme in German macOS). {dmg}, {zip}, {exe}, {flag}, {tar}, {binary}, {home}, {windows}: file names and commands, placed where the sentence needs them.
help.macos.sequoia: macOS 15 Sequoia and newer: open the app once and click Done. Then open System Settings › Privacy & Security, scroll to "SpaceCorps 2027" was blocked and click Open Anyway.
help.macos.older: macOS 12 to 14: right-click (or Control-click) the app, choose Open, then Open again.
@help.macos.terminal: Followed by a command to copy.
help.windows.title: Windows: "Windows protected your PC"
@help.windows.title: Quote the SmartScreen window's title as Windows writes it in your language.
help.windows.extract: Right-click the {zip}, choose Extract All, and open the SpaceCorps 2027 folder. The whole game is in spacecorps2027.exe.
help.windows.run: Start {exe}. If SmartScreen appears, click More info, then Run anyway.
help.linux.title: Linux: make the AppImage executable
help.linux.chmod: Mark it executable, then start it (or use your file manager's Properties › Allow executing as program):
@help.linux.chmod: Followed by a command to copy.
help.linux.fuse: No FUSE on your system? Run it with {flag}, or take the {tar}: unpack it and start {binary}.

help.verify.text: Compare the file's SHA-256 with the one listed above:
help.server.title: Game server
help.server.connects: The game connects to {url} {status}. To play on another SpaceCorps server, click Change server under the login card, or go to Settings › Account › Server.
@help.server.connects: {url} is the server's address, {status} its state in brackets (status.inline.wrap). Change server is the game's landing.server.change: use its translation.
help.server.files: Your login and settings are kept in {home} ({windows} on Windows).
@copy.done: Screen reader label of a copy button for a moment after it copied.
